summary: Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Shenphen Nangwa.
Oriane Lavolé works in Buddhist and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University as a PhD candidate and doctoral student, attested from 2020 to 2026.

Orion Klautau specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned a B.A. from the University of São Paulo and a Ph.D. from Tohoku University, where he was appointed Associate Professor in 2015.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Orna Almogi studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, and completed her doctorate under David P. Jackson and Lambert Schmithausen. Her posts include the University of Hamburg and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, Osamu Hayashima studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg. He held professorships at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science (attested 2003–2013), and Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2015).
Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Japanology. He held posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology. After studying at Kansai University from circa 1948 to 1953, he held posts at Kansai University (~1954–1997), Kogakkan University (~1997–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata specialized in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology after studying under Baiei Henmi. He held positions at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and the Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Linguist Osborn Bergin studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning, and the University of Freiburg under Kuno Meyer and Heinrich Zimmer. He held academic posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and the Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940–1941).
Oscar Botto was an Indology scholar who studied under Mario Vallauri and founded the journal Indologica Taurinensia.

Oscar Flex worked in linguistics and Indology. He served as a missionary for the Gossner Evangelical Lutheran Church in 1861, worked with the Society for the Propagation of the Gospel in Foreign Parts in 1877, and was a superintendent for the East-India Tea Company.

Oscar Lewis was an Indology scholar who earned his B.A. at the City College of New York and his Ph.D. at Columbia University. He held positions at Brooklyn College, Washington University in St. Louis, the University of Washington, and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign.

Linguist and Indologist Oscar Luis Chavarria-Aguilar earned degrees from UC Berkeley and the University of Pennsylvania. He held posts at Deccan College, the American University in Cairo, the University of Michigan, the University of Rochester, CCNY, and the National University of Costa Rica.

Indologist and linguist Oskar Frankfurter studied at Humboldt University of Berlin and the University of Göttingen. He founded the Siam Society in 1904, directed the National Library of Thailand (1905–1917), and taught Thai at the University of Hamburg (1921–1922).

Linguist Oskar Johann Wiedemann studied at the University of Tartu from 1879 to 1889, earning his Magister and Ph.D. and studying under Leo Meyer. He subsequently served as a Privatdozent at the University of Tartu from 1887 to 1890.

Oskar Kressler was a scholar of Japanology and Indology who studied at Leipzig, Geneva, and Strasbourg under Ernst Windisch and Ernst Leumann. He later served as a Privatdozent and extraordinary professor of Japanology at the University of Bonn between 1932 and 1949.

Indologist and linguist Oskar von Hinüber studied at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg under Karl Hoffmann and Paul Thieme. He served as a professor at the University of Freiburg from 1981 to 2006 and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served as Emeritus Director at CNRS and Adjunct Professor of Central and South Asian Art, Archaeology, and Numismatics at UC Berkeley (~2012).

Osvald Sirén was a scholar of Sinology, history, and archaeology who completed his doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki. He held positions at Stockholm University, Harvard, Yale, the Guimet Museum, and the Nationalmuseum.
